newsitem.title: CANADA: Midland Walwyn CEO says firm not for sale.
newsitem.headline: Midland Walwyn CEO says firm not for sale.

text.p: Midland Walwyn Inc, Canada's last big independent investment dealer, said on Tuesday that it was not for sale and suggested the probability of a hostile takeover bid was low.
Midland Walwyn's stock has been volatile in recent weeks due to market rumors that a bid may materialize for the Toronto-based firm.

"The fact is we are not for sale. We are fully committed to independence. If you didn't understand that, hopefully you're getting that message now," Midland Walwyn chief executive Robert Schultz told an analysts' meeting.
Midland operates Midland Walwyn Capital Inc, the last major brokerage not controlled by Canada's six big banks.
Speculation that Midland Walwyn may be on the block has persisted since Royal Bank of Canada moved to acquire Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd, the only other big independent dealer, in August.

Midland Walwyn shares climbed steadily from around 9.50 when the Richardson takeover was announced on August 29. The stock hit a 52-week high of 12.75 about two weeks ago when the market was rife with rumors that Bank of Nova Scotia unit ScotiaMcLeod Inc would make an offer.
The rumors were denied by officials with Midland and the bank. Midland stock has eased from its recent highs. It was off 0.25 to 11.50 today on 52,000 shares in Toronto.
Aside from ScotiaMcLeod, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and CT Financial Services Inc 's Canada Trustco Mortgage Co have been mentioned as potential bidders for Midland.

Schultz said a hostile takeover would be difficult and pricey. "We certainly feel that we could demonstrate that staying the course is probably better for shareholders so a hostile takeover would be very difficult," he said.
Schultz noted that some industry observers have said that Richardson Greenshields' C$480 million price tag was pricey. Royal Bank is expected to close the deal on November 1.
"We think it (Midland Walwyn's price) would even be higher because of the scarcity value," Schultz said.
"If we want to stay this course and this philosophy, we must continue to produce good operating results and build shareholder value," he said.
Midland Walwyn's earnings climbed 29 percent to C$0.19 a share in the third quarter. Revenues rose 16 percent to C$145 million in the quarter.
Schultz said Midland Walwyn was on track for revenues exceeding C$600 million this year. The company posted 1995 revenues of C$519 million.
Midland Walwyn's investment in trainees in recent years was expected to start paying off in 1997, said chief financial officer Bill Fulton.

"We have about 400 people in the network that have been trained over the last three or four years. We anticipate that will increase our revenue by between C$20 (million) and C$25 million next year," Fulton said. That would boost pre-tax earnings by about C$10 million next year, he said.
